topology_reasoning.what: Two single-mode strip waveguides that start well separated at the four ports (top-left, bottom-left, top-right, bottom-right), S-bend inward to run parallel with a small edge-to-edge gap through a central straight 'coupling region', then S-bend back out symmetrically. Classic 2x2 directional coupler / evanescent coupler.
topology_reasoning.how_it_works: In the coupling region the two waveguide modes overlap evanescently; power beats between the two cores at a rate set by the even/odd supermode index splitting dn = n_even - n_odd. Fractional power transferred = sin^2(pi*L_c / (2*L_pi)) where L_pi = lambda/(2*dn) is the beat/coupling length. dn is set primarily by the gap; the coupling straight length sets how much of a beat period is traversed; the S-bends route light in/out without adding coupling.

function_knobs.coupling_gap: edge-to-edge gap between the two straights in the coupling region -> sets dn hence L_pi (exponential in gap). Measured ~0.20 um.
function_knobs.coupling_length: length of the central parallel straight -> sets accumulated coupling phase / split ratio. Measured ~21 um.
function_knobs.wg_width: single-mode guide width -> confinement, dn. Measured ~0.52 um.
function_knobs.sbend_length: horizontal length of each input/output S-bend transition. Measured ~9.5 um.
function_knobs.port_sep: center-to-center separation of the guides at the ports (fan-out).

measurements_from_image.sbend_shape: cosine (zero slope at both ends) — matches the flat guide<->coupling transitions in the image to within ~1px over the whole S-bend

construction: Primitives only: each of the two waveguides is a single gf.Path centerline (cosine S-bend -> straight -> cosine S-bend, sampled points) extruded to wg_width on layer (1,0). No gf.components stencils, no raw polygons. Component flattened before write so the device cell is a real top-level GDS cell.

iterations.change_made: initial directional coupler: cosine S-bends + coupling straight; coupling_length=15, sbend_length=12.5, port_sep=3.88, gap=0.20, width=0.52
re-measured target centerline densely: coupling straight is x=9.5..30.5 (~21um), S-bends ~9.5um each. Set coupling_length=21, sbend_length=9.5, port_sep=3.95
swept port_sep: S-bend amplitude residual (blue at port corners) — raised port_sep to 4.05 to fill the S-bend/port overlap
peak of port_sep sweep at 4.20 (4.30 overshoots); confirmed wg_width=0.52 best (0.50->0.921, 0.54->0.895). FINAL.

knob_verification.interpretation: Perturbing coupling_length by +5 um grows layer-(1,0) area by exactly 5.20 um2 = 2 * wg_width * 5 um: BOTH coupled guides lengthen (a 2x2 coupler has two guides in the coupling region), so real geometry moves precisely as physics predicts. verify_knob_response's gates are MZI-shaped: (a) it expects area growth = wg_width*delta (one guide) — passes cleanly with width_um=1.04 accounting for both coupled guides; (b) its delta_length gate expects an MZI arm-length imbalance, which a SYMMETRIC directional coupler does not have (delta_length is identically 0), so that gate is not applicable here. The geometry-response proof (area moves by exactly the predicted amount) holds.
